invariants: The storyboard preserves script dac-us-24-mornings-script-v1 version 1.1.0 and the approved concept.
All shots form one continuous non-overlapping timeline from 0 through 50 seconds.
Every shot remains inside the time range of its parent script beat.
Every approved spoken line appears verbatim once in the storyboard and remains in script order; continuation shots add no new words.
Every shot has exactly one allowed source strategy and at least one stable asset requirement.
Every asset separates requirement status, access state, and inspection state; an observed page image is not treated as a supplied file.
A REQUIRED_PRODUCTION_ASSET gap blocks only the affected production job, not storyboard or claim approval.
No visual invents a product feature, figure design, customer reaction, testimonial, objective claim, or commercial value absent from approved inputs.
A complete 24-figure lineup is shown only when a faithful source exists; otherwise the growing-collection fallback is used.
Ornament use relies on a faithful source or the static page-claim fallback rather than an invented mechanism.
The $35.90 price, free standard shipping on orders $49+, and 30-day returns remain editable overlays and retain their launch-time verification rules.
The $35.90 single item is never implied to qualify for free standard shipping.
Platform provider, aspect ratio, resolution, frame rate, clip limits, prompt syntax, and API behavior remain UNBOUND when no verified profile is supplied.
Provider prompt and payload fields remain null; the Storyboard Director does not generate media or submit platform jobs.
Every storyboard shot is assigned to exactly one provider-neutral job unit and job-unit durations sum to 50 seconds.
The final frame matches the approved AIP opening state: the same calendar with one closed numbered door ready to tap.
Markdown and JSON agree on shot IDs, timing, voiceover mapping, on-screen copy, source strategies, asset IDs, gaps, and final status.
